title: Solidarity, Security and Peace – The Israel-Hamas Conflict
what_it_is: Solidarity, Security and Peace – The Israel-Hamas Conflict

sections.label: Israel-Hamas conflict debate ruling
sections.summary: The Speaker will allow Supplementary Questions at the end of the Motion debate and gives details of the 7 October 2023 Hamas attack and Gaza death toll.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Before I call Member, Mr Vikram Nair, to move his Motion, I wish to inform Members who asked the more than 40 Parliamentary Questions (PQs) on the Israel-Hamas conflict that I will give ample opportunity for all of you to ask any Supplementary Questions at the end of the debate on the Motion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: I am making this ruling, so this is to ensure the orderly flow of debate on the Motion and to enable all Members to make your speeches without disruption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: I will also allow other Members the opportunity to raise their clarifications after all Members have spoken.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: On 7 October 2023, Israel was attacked by air, land and sea by Hamas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This included a physical invasion into Israeli territory and rocket attacks, killing more than 1,200 people in Israel, and with more than 200 being taken prisoner and held as hostages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: According to both the Reuters and BBC, the civilian death toll in the Gaza is more than 9,000.

sections.label: UN resolution ES 10-21
sections.summary: The UN passed resolution ES 10-21 calling for an immediate, durable and sustained humanitarian truce leading to a cessation of hostilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The UN has since passed resolution ES 10-21, which calls for an immediate, durable and sustained humanitarian truce leading to a cessation of hostilities.

sections.label: Proposed Motion amendments
sections.summary: The Speaker wanted to amend the Motion to support UN resolution ES 10-21 and to clarify unhindered access for UN agencies, the International Red Cross and other international organisations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: As these are important developments, I had wanted to amend the Motion to include a specific limb for this house to support the UN resolution ES 10-21 as well as to amend limb (b) to clarify that unhindered access should be given to UN agencies, the International Red Cross and other international organisations to provide humanitarian support.

sections.label: Humanitarian aid and international law
sections.summary: Steps should be taken to facilitate humanitarian aid reaching civilians, and both parties should consider international humanitarian law during the conflict.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Steps should be taken to facilitate humanitarian aid reaching the civilian population and both parties should take into account international humanitarian law when conducting the conflict.

sections.label: Hamas hostages and Geneva Conventions
sections.summary: Hamas continues to hold more than 200 civilians hostage from its 7 October invasion of Israel, violating Common Article 3 of the Geneva Conventions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Next, Hamas continues to hold more than 200 civilians hostage from its invasion of Israel on 7 October.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The taking of hostages is a violation of Common Article 3 of the Geneva Conventions.

sections.label: Alex Yam proposed Motion amendments
sections.summary: Mr Alex Yam will propose amendments to this limb to reiterate that parties must comply with positive obligations under international law, including minimising war effects on civilians.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: My colleague, Mr Alex Yam, will be proposing some amendments to this limb of the Motion to expressly reiterate that parties must comply with the positive obligations under international law, including to minimise the effects of war on the civilian population.

sections.label: Middle East peace framework
sections.summary: A framework for Middle East peace included Palestinian self-government in the West Bank and Gaza and a peace treaty framework between Israel, Egypt and other Arab nations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Here, a framework for peace in the Middle East was agreed upon, with a process for Palestinian self-government in the West Bank and Gaza and a framework for conclusion of a peace treaty between Israel, Egypt and other Arab nations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This paved the way for the peace treaty between Egypt and Israel, in which Israel returned the Sinai Peninsula to Egypt and Egypt opened the Suez Canal to Israeli ships.

sections.label: Interim Palestinian government accords
sections.summary: An agreement set up an interim Palestinian government for five years and a framework for phased Israeli withdrawal, with Palestinian authorities building a stronger police force for internal security.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: An agreement was reached for the setting up of an interim Palestinian government for five years, during which unresolved issues would be addressed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: These accords also provided a framework for the withdrawal in phases of the Israeli armed forces from Palestinian territory, with Israel retaining responsibility for protecting the territories from air and sea attack but with the Palestinian authorities setting up a stronger police force to take over the responsibilities for internal security.

sections.label: Hamas attack and two-state solution
sections.summary: The Hamas attack on Israel adds legitimacy to Israel's security concerns and may set back Palestinian statehood, so both should refocus on the two-state solution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Unfortunately, this latest attack by Hamas on Israel adds to the legitimacy of Israel's security concerns and may set back the journey to Palestinian statehood even further.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Both should refocus on achieving the two-state solution, where the two people can live together securely.

sections.label: Singapore racial and religious harmony
sections.summary: In Singapore, racial and religious harmony is something worked hard over the years to develop.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In Singapore, our racial and religious harmony is one that we have worked hard over the years to develop.

sections.label: Common ground and tolerance
sections.summary: Maintaining peace requires common ground and tolerance, and many share an understanding that both Palestinians and Jewish people have a right to peaceful existence and a nation of their own.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In order to maintain this peace, we need to find common ground and tolerance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: We need to look for things that bring us together rather than differences that divide us.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I think many of us share an understanding that both the Palestinians and Jewish people have a right to peaceful existence and a nation of their own.

sections.label: Motion amendment and UN resolution
sections.summary: Procedurally a Motion cannot be amended by its mover, and this includes Singapore's vote supporting UN Emergency Session Resolution ES-10/21 calling for an immediate humanitarian truce leading to a cessation of hostilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Mr Vikram Nair, you are correct that procedurally, you cannot amend your own Motion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Can I have a copy of your amendment?

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: This includes Singapore's vote in support of the UN Emergency Session Resolution ES-10/21, which calls for an immediate humanitarian truce leading to a cessation of hostilities.

sections.label: Hamas October attack called terrorism
sections.summary: The passage states that what Hamas perpetrated on 7 October is terrorism, plain and simple.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: To call a spade a spade, what Hamas perpetrated on 7 October, is terrorism, plain and simple.

sections.label: Gaza death toll and division
sections.summary: Israeli troops encircle Gaza City and divided Gaza into North and South, with the death toll rising to an unverified 9,227.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: Even as Israeli troops encircle Gaza City and late last night – they have divided Gaza into North and South Gaza – the death toll has risen to an as yet unverified 9,227, of which an estimated 40% are children, 65% if you include women.

sections.label: Singapore UN resolution support
sections.summary: Singapore voted in favour of the 27 October 2023 Emergency Session Resolution on protecting civilians and upholding legal and humanitarian obligations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: Most recently, as I quoted earlier, the Emergency Session Resolution on 27 October 2023 in which we voted in favour of a resolution titled "Protection of civilians and upholding legal and humanitarian obligations".

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: Our Permanent Representative to the UN, Ambassador Burhan, explained our support that despite registering our regret for the omissions in the said Motion as Singapore has "always been a consistent advocate and defender of international law, the UN Charter and the rules-based multilateral system".

sections.label: Votes back two-state solution
sections.summary: By voting in alignment with those principles, Singapore emphasises its stance on a negotiated two-state solution and international law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: By consistently casting our vote in alignment with those principles, we emphasise our unwavering stance on the importance of a negotiated two-state solution and the need for all parties to act within the bounds of international law.

sections.label: Multi-religious harmony pledge
sections.summary: The Government's pledge to safeguard Singapore's multi-religious harmony remains unwavering.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: The Government's pledge to safeguard our multi-religious harmony remains unwavering.

sections.label: Online misinformation targeting Singapore
sections.summary: Since 7 October, online traffic and misinformation targeting Singapore and its local population has risen exponentially.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: Let us not kid ourselves, all it takes is a cursory search and you will see that since the 7 October, online traffic and misinformation targeting Singapore and our local population has been on an exponential rise.

sections.label: Amendments to Israel-Gaza Motion
sections.summary: Five substantive amendments and one consequential amendment by Mr Alex Yam to the Motion are listed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: Let us unite our voices in the collective call for a safer and more harmonious world and for a resolution to the current conflict in Israel and the Gaza.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: There are five substantive amendments proposed by Member Mr Alex Yam to the Motion and a consequential amendment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: They are: Amendment No 1, "After line 4, to insert a new part with the words 'Supports UN Resolution ES-10/21, which calls for an immediate, durable and sustained humanitarian truce leading to a cessation of hostilities'"; Amendment No 2, "In line 5, the words 'and unhindered access to United Nations humanitarian agencies, the International Red Cross and other humanitarian organisations' be added at the end"; Amendment No 3, "In line 7, after the word 'Calls', to delete the word 'for' and insert 'on'"; Amendment No 4, "In line 7, after the words 'all parties to', to insert the following: 'comply fully with international humanitarian law, including to'"; Amendment No 5, "In line 7, to delete 'including the release of all hostages' and insert 'release all hostages and minimise the effects of combat on the civilian population'".

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: And if the new part is agreed to, Mr Alex Yam's consequential amendment is to "rename the current parts from (b) – (f) to (c) – (g)".

sections.label: Question on Alex Yam's amendments
sections.summary: The Question is put on the amendments as moved by Mr Alex Yam.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: "The Question is the amendments as moved by Mr Alex Yam".

sections.label: Condemning violence against civilians
sections.summary: The speaker rejects violence against civilians, citing deaths on 7 October and in Gaza.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We must reject and condemn violence against the innocent and any civilian.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: There is no justification for what has happened on 7 October, amongst those killed are citizens from other countries including those from our close neighbours in ASEAN: 18 Thai nationals killed with another 11 taken hostage, seven Filipinos missing and one Cambodian student killed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In Gaza, out of the almost 9,000 people reportedly dead, more than 3,600 were children killed in the first 25 days.

sections.label: Support for Singapore's UN vote
sections.summary: The speaker supports Singapore's 28 October vote for a UN resolution on a humanitarian truce and aid access.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: As such, I support the Singapore Government's actions on 28 October to vote in favour of the UN General Assembly Resolution calling for, among other things, a humanitarian truce and aid access to the besieged Gaza Strip.

sections.label: Palestinian officials trained under ETAP
sections.summary: MFA updated that since 2013 over 700 Palestinian Authority officials and students benefited from ETAP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) updated that since 2013, more than 700 Palestinian Authority officials and students have benefited through the Enhanced Technical Assistance Programme (ETAP) training courses and study visits to Singapore.

sections.label: UN inquiry and vaccination proposal
sections.summary: A UN Commission of Inquiry has collected evidence of war crimes since 7 October 2023, and the speaker hopes Singapore considers vaccinations and medication for Palestinians.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In this regard, the UN has already constituted an Independent International Commission of Inquiry which has been collecting and preserving evidence of war crimes since 7 October 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Thirdly, besides the current assistance pledged by the Singapore Government, I hope that Singapore can also perhaps consider providing critical vaccinations and other medication for the Palestinian population who are facing a health crisis.

sections.label: Faith, ceasefire, UN inquiry
sections.summary: The speaker says practising faith shows compassion, hopes foreign Muslim workers join, and supports a UN-voted humanitarian ceasefire and UN Commission of Inquiry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This is not only a way to practice our faith, but it also demonstrates to everyone that our religion teaches us to give emphasis to compassion, peace and humanity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I hope we can do more to also make the call to our foreign Muslim workers who are working here, so that they also understand our ways and become part of this effort in Singapore Globally, I hope the Government will also support a humanitarian ceasefire as voted by the UN, so that basic aid can be allowed to continue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I also support the Commission of Inquiry that is set up by the UN to gather and preserve evidence of war crimes, and investigate allegations of international law violations.

sections.label: Palestinian aspirations and lasting peace
sections.summary: The passage states that Palestinian aspirations, pain and suffering cannot be ignored for longstanding peace, and that peace cannot come through cycles of violence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The one thing that this tragedy proves to us is this – the Palestinians people's aspirations, pain and suffering cannot be ignored if we want longstanding peace and stability for both Israelis and Palestinians to live side by side and prosper together.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Longstanding peace cannot be achieved through a cycle of violence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It is broken through the intervention of love, humanity and compassion.

sections.label: US aid leverage and casualties
sections.summary: The passage says Israeli declarations are toothless without American endorsement, that cutting US aid could stop settlements, and that thousands have been killed since 7 October.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Israelis, however, know that such declarations are toothless unless they are endorsed by the Americans." "If, for example, the Americans are willing to cut off financial aid to Israel amounting to $115 billion since 1949 as well as other forms of military and political support until the building of settlements stops, Israel will have no choice but to act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The cause is kept alive across the Middle East as well as in other parts of Asia through television images that play up Palestinian sufferings." Mr Speaker, since 7 October, thousands of innocents have been killed and wounded in Israel and Gaza.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Among those are thousands of children, the overwhelming majority of which are Palestinian.

sections.label: Return of Israeli hostages
sections.summary: The passage calls for the immediate return of all Israeli hostages captured in Hamas' military operation in Southern Israel on 7 October 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: At the same time, we call for the immediate return of all Israeli hostages captured in Hamas' military operation in Southern Israel on 7 October 2023.

sections.label: Previous Israel-Hamas violence deaths
sections.summary: The passage reports that in previous bouts of violence, 5,365 Palestinians and 308 Israelis were reported killed, many of them children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In previous bouts of violence between Israel and Hamas, 5,365 Palestinians are reported to have been killed, many of them children, while 308 Israelis are reported to have lost their lives.

sections.label: Expected Gaza death toll
sections.summary: The passage states that, if history is a guide, dead Palestinians in Gaza will soon cross 10,000, many being women and children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: If history is a guide, we will soon see the number of dead Palestinians in Gaza cross the 10,000 mark, with many of the dead being women and children.

sections.label: WP ceasefire and two-state call
sections.summary: The WP statement calls for an immediate ceasefire, return of hostages, humanitarian aid to Gaza, and negotiations towards a two-state solution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This sad reality repeats itself ad infinitum, scuttling both the birth of a viable Palestinian state as well as creating conditions in Israel where its borders are secure and its people live in peace with their neighbours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: These are the reasons that explain why the WP statement calls for an immediate ceasefire, a return of hostages and the conveyance of humanitarian aid to the Gaza Strip, to be followed by serious negotiations towards a two-state solution.

sections.label: Singaporean's planned synagogue attack
sections.summary: The Internal Security Department said the Israel-Palestinian conflict was one reason a 20-year-old Singaporean planned to attack Jews at Maghain Aboth Synagogue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The long-standing Israel-Palestinian conflict was, according to the Internal Security Department, one of the reasons why a 20-year-old Singaporean was remanded some two years ago, because he planned to attack and murder Jews worshipping at the Maghain Aboth Synagogue, the oldest synagogue in Singapore.

sections.label: WP backs UN truce decision
sections.summary: The WP supports Singapore's UN General Assembly decision calling for an immediate and sustained humanitarian truce leading to a cessation of hostilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To that end, the WP supports the major decision taken by Singapore at the UN General Assembly, which is referred to in the amended Motion, calling for an immediate and sustained humanitarian truce, leading to a cessation of hostilities.

sections.label: WP supports Geneva Conventions
sections.summary: The WP supports the Geneva Conventions and their additional protocols that prescribe international humanitarian law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The WP supports the Geneva Conventions and their additional protocols that prescribe international humanitarian law.

sections.label: Small states need international law
sections.summary: Singapore is a small state that relies on international law, and small states need international law and their protections.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Singapore is a small state that relies on international law, and small states need international law and their protections.

sections.label: Singapore vote on Jerusalem
sections.summary: In the Israel-Palestinian dispute, Singapore voted in the UN against calls to recognise Jerusalem as Israel's capital.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the context of the Israel-Palestinian dispute, Singapore has voted in the UN against calls for Jerusalem to be recognised as the capital of Israel.

sections.label: Middle East Quartet two-state solution
sections.summary: The Middle East Quartet recognised two states for two peoples, and the WP backs this as the only feasible path to resolution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To conclude, Mr Speaker, about two decades ago, a grouping called the Middle East Quartet, made up of the United States, the European Union, Russia and the United Nations, has recognised that in order to have peace, it is necessary to fulfil the aspirations of the two parties for an independent homeland through two states for two peoples – the state of Israel and an independent viable state of Palestine, both of which must be able to live in peace and security.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The WP backs this stand, which is also that of the Government of Singapore, as the only feasible path to a durable, just and comprehensive resolution to the Israel-Palestine conflict.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Today, this prospect may feel far removed, but until that day comes, it is important that Singapore advocates strongly for the safety and security of civilians and children who are the innocent victims of this long-standing conflict.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We call on both Israeli and Palestinian leadership to make compromises for peace, to prevent future generations from paying for the actions of their elders – I should say, actions and omissions of their elders.

sections.label: Gaza health ministry casualty figures
sections.summary: The Gaza health ministry released figures that thousands have died and even more were injured.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The Gaza health ministry has released figures that thousands have died, even more injured.

sections.label: Gaza civilians restricted access
sections.summary: Civilians in Gaza were restricted access to food, water, electricity and communications, and aid was prevented from entering.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Civilians in Gaza were restricted access to food, water, electricity, communications, and aid was prevented from entering.

sections.label: Singaporeans humanitarian assistance efforts
sections.summary: Singaporeans joined hands in humanitarian assistance, including medical supplies, a mass prayer session, and a fundraising campaign collecting over S$4.6 million.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Apart from making comments, sharing videos and showing photos on social media, Singaporeans have also banded together to act collectively.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We witnessed how Singaporeans from all walks of life have joined hands in efforts to provide humanitarian assistance – from supplying medical paraphernalia with Humanity Matters on 29 October, to the special mass prayer session organised by Pergas and mosques across Singapore, as well as a fundraising campaign by Rahmatan Lil Alamin Foundation (RLAF) which managed to collect more than S$4.6 million within two weeks, and other community-based efforts by groups, such as Chendol Kita and Fabmarket, which have used their own platforms to contribute to local efforts.

sections.label: Singapore UN votes on Palestine
sections.summary: Singapore supported the Palestinian right to a homeland and the two-state solution, and voted for Palestine in various resolutions including for an immediate ceasefire.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: At the UN General Assembly, Singapore supported the right of the Palestinian people to a homeland and the two-state solution that was agreed by both sides through negotiations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We have also voted in favour of Palestine in various resolutions, including those in 1967 after the Six-Day War, in 1997 and 2003 against Israel in connection with the construction of the Har Homa settlement, and demanded that Israel stop the construction of the West Bank Wall, and the latest on October 27, for an immediate ceasefire, so that humanitarian aid can be extended.

sections.label: Singapore vote UN resolution ES-10/21
sections.summary: On 27 October at the UN General Assembly, Singapore voted for UN resolution ES-10/21.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: (In English): Sir, on 27 October at the UN General Assembly, Singapore voted for UN resolution ES-10/21.

sections.label: Packing Gaza relief supplies
sections.summary: The speaker and about a hundred Singaporeans packed about eight tonnes of relief supplies for Gaza with Humanity Matters.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Two weeks ago, I and around a hundred Singaporeans from all walks of life, spend time with Humanity Matters, packing about eight tonnes worth of relief supplies to Gaza.

sections.label: Rabbi and Mufti exchange respect
sections.summary: Rabbi Mordechai Abergel and Mufti Dr Nazirudin Nasir address each other with respect, express condolences and prayers, and call for permanent peace.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Rabbi Mordechai Abergel and Mufti Dr Nazirudin Nasir address each other with respect, express condolences and prayers for innocent lives taken unjustly and have called for a permanent peace.

sections.label: Calls to end Gaza violence
sections.summary: People worldwide use their voices, and the speaker appeals for an immediate cessation of violence in Gaza and the West Bank.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: With people of all ages, various backgrounds, faiths, all over the world, using our voice some in protest, some in prayer, donations, to converse, to listen, to bear witness to this crisis.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We do what we can and here in this Chamber, we understand the desire for statehood and safety of the Palestinians and the Israelis.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We use our voices to call for the indiscriminate killing of innocent civilians to end.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: And I end with a solemn appeal for parties to abide by the humanitarian truth for an immediate cessation of the violence in Gaza and the West Bank and for justice to prevail.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The killing of 1,400 people, most of them civilians in Israel and the taking of over 240 hostages by Hamas on 7 October 2023 cannot be justified and must be unequivocally condemned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Since 7 October, more than 9,770 people in Gaza including thousands of children have been killed according to the health officials in Gaza.

sections.label: WP supports UN resolution vote
sections.summary: The WP supports Singapore's vote on the 26 October UN General Assembly resolution calling for a humanitarian truce and release of captives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The WP supports Singapore's vote on the resolution at the UN General Assembly on 26 October which among other things, call for an immediate durable and sustained humanitarian truce leading to cessation of hostilities, as well as the immediate and unconditional release of all civilians being illegally held captive.

sections.label: Singapore aid package for Palestinians
sections.summary: In 2016, Singapore pledged to double the enhanced technical assistance package for Palestinian officials to $10 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In 2016, Singapore pledged a double, the enhanced technical assistance package for Palestinian officials to the quantum of $10 million.

sections.label: Safe avenues for political debate
sections.summary: Political debate in Parliament, classrooms or the Speakers' Corner gives Singaporeans a safe avenue to discuss international conflicts including Israel-Palestine.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Political debate occurring within Parliament, in classrooms or at the Speakers' Corner provides Singaporeans with a safe avenue to express their views and engage in discussions about international conflicts, including about the Israel-Palestine situation.

sections.label: Classroom discussions on this topic
sections.summary: Schools and higher education institutions should promote classroom discussions so young people can voice views and respect different viewpoints.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Schools and Institutions of Higher Education should more actively promote classroom discussions on this topic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This will not only provide young people with a platform to voice their perspectives and express their frustrations with the situation but also encourage them to respect different viewpoints.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In our era, where information is widely accessible, there is no excuse for not acquiring a basic grasp of this important issue.

sections.label: Compliance with international humanitarian law
sections.summary: The speaker agrees with the Motion's call for all parties to comply with international humanitarian law and protect civilians.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I have residents who are concerned and have asked if these actions comply with international humanitarian law in war.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: So, I agree with the Motion – (e) calling on all parties to comply fully with international humanitarian law, including ensuring the safety and security of civilians, release all civilian hostages and minimize the effects of combat on the civilian population.

sections.label: Local fund collections for relief
sections.summary: Islamic Relief, Singapore Red Cross and RLAF run fund collections, with RLAF raising over S$4.6 million in two weeks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: For example, Islamic Relief, the Singapore Red Cross and RLAF are running ongoing fund collections.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I am proud of the local community's speedy and generous response to RLAF's fund collection efforts, raising more than S$4.6 million in only 2 weeks, as mentioned earlier by my Parliamentary colleague Ms Nadia.

sections.label: Support for immediate humanitarian truce
sections.summary: The speaker supports the Motion's limb (b) calling for an immediate, durable and sustained humanitarian truce leading to cessation of hostilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: As such, for a start, I support the Motion's limb (b), which calls for an immediate, durable and sustained humanitarian truce leading to a cessation of hostilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: While the politics of the region are extremely fraught and complex, Singapore must continue to urge all parties involved to prioritise and protect human life and seek political concessions at the bargaining table rather than through warfare.

sections.label: Government aid to local organisations
sections.summary: The question asks how the Government ensured its $300,000 aid donation goes to the right local organisations instead of fuelling conflict.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: How has the Government ensured that the $300,000 it has donated in aid so far will be going to the right local organisations instead of fuelling the ongoing conflict?

sections.label: Middle East conflict recession risk
sections.summary: Economists warn that escalated Israel-Hamas fighting could tip the world into recession and affect commodity prices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Economists have sounded concerns that an escalation in the fighting between Israel and Hamas could possibly tip the world into recession in a worst-case scenario.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Similar to the Russia-Ukraine war, major conflict in the Middle East could have far-reaching price effects across a range of commodity prices.

sections.label: Diplomatic push for political solutions
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Singaporean Government to do more diplomatically to help realise political solutions to the ongoing conflict.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: They do not deserve to live in tragedy, generation after generation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I urge the Singaporean Government to step up our efforts to do more on the diplomatic front to help realise political solutions to the ongoing conflict.

sections.label: Protecting civilians and hostages
sections.summary: It states Israeli and Palestinian civilian lives must be protected, supports UN Resolution ES-10/21, and calls for Hamas to return hostages and for a ceasefire.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The lives of both Israeli and Palestinian civilians must be protected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We strongly support the United Nations Resolution ES-10/21 on October 28 calling for a humanitarian truce leading to a cessation of hostilities in the Gaza Strip.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We call for Hamas to immediately and unconditionally return all civilian hostages safely to their families and to facilitate a ceasefire and for Israel to respond favourably to such a move if it happens.

sections.label: Two-state solution and education
sections.summary: PSP supports a two-state solution based on UN Security Resolutions and urges the Government to enhance education on Israeli-Palestinian history.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: PSP supports Singapore's long-held position that just, enduring and comprehensive peace in the Middle East must be based on a two-state solution based on relevant UN Security Resolutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It is also an issue that is of interest to the main communities of our society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We urge the Government to enhance education on the Israeli-Palestinian history in the future so that Singaporeans can have more accurate and complete information on the conflict.

sections.label: Solidarity, truce and humanitarian aid
sections.summary: It says condemning violence upholds justice, compassion and human rights, notes voting with 119 countries, calls for a humanitarian truce, and commends Singaporeans' aid.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: By condemning acts of violence, we stand up for the values of justice, compassion and human rights that our citizens hold dear.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We stood in solidarity with 119 other countries by voting in favour of the United Stations General Assembly Resolution.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As included in the amendment to this Motion, we call for an immediate durable and sustained humanitarian truce, leading to a cessation of hostilities.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Regardless of our background and differences, I believe we stand by our national pledge to be one united people in our reaction to this deepening humanitarian crisis.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We recognise that the situation in Gaza is a massive humanitarian crisis and it is commendable that Singaporeans have come together in solidarity as a nation to provide humanitarian aid and donations.

sections.label: Advocating negotiated two-state solution
sections.summary: It states the nation must advocate a peaceful resolution aligned with a negotiated two-state solution consistent with UN Security Council Resolutions.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As a nation, we must advocate for a peaceful resolution to this conflict, align with our commitment to a negotiated two-state solution consistent with the relevant United Nations Security Council Resolutions.

sections.label: Hamas attack and hostages in Gaza
sections.summary: It states more than 1,000 militants infiltrated Israeli territory, killing more than 1,400 persons, and Hamas abducted more than 200 civilians held as hostages in Gaza.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: At the same time, more than 1,000 militants infiltrated Israeli territory and killed more than 1,400 persons.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Hamas also abducted more than 200 civilians including senior citizens, women and children, who today are held as hostages in Gaza.

sections.label: Singapore condemns Hamas attack
sections.summary: Singapore condemns the Hamas terrorist attack and calls for the safe, immediate and unconditional release of all civilian hostages.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: These acts of indiscriminate killing, torture and kidnapping of innocent civilians are acts of terror.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: This is why Singapore has strongly condemned the terrorist attack by Hamas and why we have called for the safe, immediate and unconditional release of all civilian hostages.

sections.label: Gaza casualties and displacement
sections.summary: Gaza health authorities estimate over 9,000 Palestinians died, many more injured, and over 1.5 million displaced without adequate shelter, food, water or medical attention.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: To date, health authorities in Gaza have estimated that more than 9,000 Palestinians, including many women and children in Gaza have died, many more have suffered injuries and over 1.5 million would have been displaced from their homes without adequate shelter, food, water or medical attention.

sections.label: Siege of Gaza prohibited
sections.summary: Holding Gaza's two million people under siege and depriving them of basic necessities would violate international law, as collective punishment is prohibited by the laws of war.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Gaza is home to some two million fellow human beings (almost half of whom are children) and it would be a grave violation of international law to hold them under siege and while doing so deprive them of basic necessities such as food and water.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: To be clear, collective punishment is prohibited by the laws of war.

sections.label: Investigating alleged humanitarian violations
sections.summary: Any alleged violation of international humanitarian law in this conflict should be investigated in accordance with international law.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Any alleged violation of international humanitarian law in this conflict should therefore be investigated in accordance with international law.

sections.label: Two-state solution position
sections.summary: Singapore upholds its long-standing position that a negotiated two-state solution, consistent with UN Security Council resolutions 242 and 338, is the only viable option.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Fifth point, Singapore continues to uphold our long-standing and consistent position that a negotiated two-state solution, consistent with relevant UN Security Council resolutions, especially 242 and 338, that a two-state solution is the only viable option for a comprehensive, just and durable solution to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

sections.label: Engaging Palestinian Authority
sections.summary: Singapore will continue engaging the Palestinian Authority and supporting its capacity-building through the Enhanced Technical Assistance Package, with exchanges and a Ramallah office opened in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: So, in the meantime, we will continue to engage the Palestinian Authority.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: We will support their capacity-building efforts through the Enhanced Technical Assistance Package.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: The Prime Minister Mohammad Shtayyeh visited Singapore last year whilst Prime Minister Lee, Senior Minister Teo Chee Hean, Minister Mohamad Maliki Osman and I have visited Ramallah, in fact, on more than one occasion.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: We opened our Singapore Representative Office in Ramallah in 2022.

sections.label: Muslim community Gaza fundraising
sections.summary: The Muslim community responded in a restrained, responsible and responsive manner, working with other communities to raise funds for humanitarian assistance for Palestinian civilians in Gaza.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Our Muslim community, in particular, have responded in a very restrained, responsible and responsive manner, working in concert with other communities to collectively raise funds for humanitarian assistance for the Palestinian civilians in Gaza.

sections.label: Singaporeans leaving Israel and Palestinian Territories
sections.summary: Singapore advised Singaporeans to leave Israel and the Palestinian Territories, facilitated departures, and thanked Australia, Canada, Portugal and Korea for evacuation help.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: On 7 October 2023, we advised Singaporeans to leave Israel and the Palestinian Territories as soon as possible.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: We reached out to Singaporeans who had registered with MFA and we facilitated the departure of those who needed assistance.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: But even today, you might be surprised to know that 40 registered Singaporeans remain in Israel and the Palestinian Territories.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: More than 120 Singaporeans heeded our advice and left by land or air earlier.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: While most Singaporeans were able to leave by commercial means, a few who were unable to do so departed via dedicated evacuation flights which were organised by other countries.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I need to express our gratitude to the governments of Australia, Canada, Portugal and Korea for helping our Singaporeans to leave Israel safely.

sections.label: Foreign policy depends on domestic cohesion
sections.summary: The Minister for Foreign Affairs says consistent foreign policy depends on domestic cohesion and consensus, and clarifies remarks on the WP's 18 October statement condemning killings of non-combatants.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I make this appeal as the Minister for Foreign Affairs that our ability to conduct consistent and coherent foreign policy in a very volatile and dangerous world depends on domestic cohesion and consensus.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: I rise to clarify some remarks made by the Minister for Foreign Affairs, specifically, his comment about the WP's statement of 18 October.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: The focus of our statement was to emphasise that whether it is Hamas, whether it is Israel, killing of non-combatants, women, children, by any country or organisation, deserves no less than absolute condemnation.

sections.label: Hamas not on list
sections.summary: The speaker states that their understanding is that Hamas is not on that list.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: My understanding is that Hamas is not on that list.

sections.label: Abstained in emergency special session vote
sections.summary: The speaker says they favoured abstaining in the vote and clarifies that the handout says they voted Yes for all emergency special session resolutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: I was in favour of abstaining in the vote.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: We abstained and the Israelis did not leave." So, I just wanted to clarify because the handout says we voted "Yes" for all these emergency special session resolutions.

sections.label: Votes against settlements in occupied territories
sections.summary: The speaker says that, as far as they know, they have voted in favour of every resolution against building settlements in occupied territories.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Specifically, on the issues of occupied territories and settlements, as far as I know, I stand ready to be corrected, we have voted in favour of every resolution that has said that they should not be building settlements in occupied territories.

sections.label: West Bank settlements and UN votes
sections.summary: Singapore says progressive settlements make a future settlement difficult and that it votes at the UN in ways that do not please the Israelis.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Yes, there is a problem in the West Bank, because of the progressive settlements, which make it very difficult for any future settlement.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: So, yes, Mr Singh, we do vote regularly at the UN in a way which does not please the Israelis, but we have a good relationship based on respect.

sections.label: Settlements, international law, terrorist act definition
sections.summary: Singapore says the settlements should not be there and breach international law, and sets out the Act's definition of a terrorist act.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Our view is that those settlements should not be there.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: If you go by the votes in the Security Council, they breach international law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: I just wish to pick up on one point that the Leader of the Opposition made.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: I think his explanation for not calling out the acts of terrorism in the initial statement was that Hamas was not a listed organisation under the Terrorism Suppression of Financing Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: There was a Schedule of the Act and Hamas is not in that Schedule, but "terrorist entity" means any entity owned or controlled by any terrorist group or group of terrorists and includes an association of such entities set out in the First Schedule.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: The second and more relevant point is that that Act sets out the definition of a terrorist act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: And a terrorist act is clearly defined as one that involves serious violence against a person, involves serious damage of property, or endangers a person's life.

sections.label: Terrorist act definition and Hamas listing
sections.summary: Singapore says the definition of a terrorist act is plainly satisfied and that Hamas is not on the list.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: There is direct violence, there is intention to compel government – the definition of terrorist act is plainly satisfied.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: I do not have the Act in front of me right now, but I know we list out specifically what some of these organisations are and the fact is, Hamas is not on that list, notwithstanding the Member's personal views to this particular issue.

sections.label: Condemnation of Hamas 7 October attacks
sections.summary: Singapore says nothing can justify what Hamas did on 7 October and the Government has strongly condemned Hamas' acts of terror.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Some have said that the attacks are justified because of the historical grievances of the Palestinians and the treatment they suffered at different times from different governments of Israel, but nothing can justify what Hamas did on 7 October.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Therefore, the Singapore Government has strongly condemned Hamas' acts of terror.

sections.label: Seed capital to Singapore Red Cross
sections.summary: The Singapore government has contributed S$300,000 as seed capital to the Singapore Red Cross.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: The Singapore government has also contributed S$300,000 as seed capital to the Singapore Red Cross (SRC).

sections.label: RLAF and SRC fundraising totals
sections.summary: The RLAF appeal for UNRWA raised over S$4.6 million and the SRC campaign raised over S$350,000 from the public.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: For example, RLAF fundraising appeal, which will be directed to the UN Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA), has raised over S$4.6 million while the SRC's fundraising campaign has also raised over S$350,000 from the public.

sections.label: Middle East aid handover trip
sections.summary: The Speaker will travel to Egypt to witness SRC aid handover to the Egyptian Red Crescent and RLAF contribution to UNRWA for Gaza.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Speaker, I will leave for the Middle East tonight and will go to Egypt to witness the handing over of humanitarian aid from SRC to the Egyptian Red Crescent Society along with the contribution of RLAF to UNRWA for Gaza.

sections.label: Singapore support for Palestinian Authority
sections.summary: Prime Minister Lee visited Ramallah in 2016 and hosted Palestinian Prime Minister Shtayyeh in 2022, with Singapore supporting PA capacity-building via a S$10 million package.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Prime Minister Lee also visited Ramallah in 2016, and hosted Palestinian Prime Minister Dr Mohammad Shtayyeh in Singapore in October 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We have and will continue to support the PA's capacity-building efforts through the S$10 million Enhanced Technical Assistance Package (ETAP).

sections.label: Singapore backs two-state solution
sections.summary: Singapore believes a negotiated two-state solution consistent with UNSC resolutions is the only viable way for Israel and Palestinians to live in peace and security.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Singapore believes that a negotiated two-state solution, consistent with relevant UNSC resolutions, remains the only viable way for Israel and Palestinians to live side-by-side in peace and security.

sections.label: Hajat Prayer at mosques
sections.summary: The Hajat Prayer held at more than 50 mosques drew over 50,000 congregants.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: The special prayer, or known as the Hajat Prayer, conducted at more than 50 mosques have attracted over 50,000 congregants.

sections.label: Schools teach discernment, not boycotts
sections.summary: Schools and IHLs continue equipping students to discern fake news and provide safe environments for civil, balanced discourse on the conflict.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We have heard calls to boycott F&B establishments.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We should not conflate the actions of governments with the operations of business and economics.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Civic literacy, critical thinking, information and media literacy skills have always been emphasised in our national curriculum.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: With the proliferation of information and diverse views across all forms of media, our schools and Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) will continue to equip students with the skills necessary to discern fake news and misinformation and build their instinct to read from credible sources and in context.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: For students who are trying to understand the ongoing conflict and navigate the multiple perspectives or wish to express their views, schools and IHLs provide a safe environment for them to engage in civil, respectful and balanced discourse and allow different opinions to be voiced and discussed objectively, even while they engage in robust and rigorous debate.

sections.label: Channel energies to practical assistance
sections.summary: Energies can be channelled constructively to provide practical assistance while appreciating Singapore's hard-earned social harmony.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Instead, we can channel our energies constructively to provide practical assistance and, at the same time, appreciating that social harmony in Singapore is hard-earned and that while it may be tested from time to time, we will always come through and stay together as Singaporeans.

sections.label: Innocent civilian lives lost
sections.summary: The speaker says we should care as fellow human beings because innocent civilian lives are being lost, and focus on saving lives and de-escalating the conflict.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Each of us care and should care because at the personal level, we are all fellow human beings, and the situation now is that numerous innocent civilian lives have been lost and are still being lost as we speak.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: We need to focus on how we can help save innocent lives and de-escalate the conflict.

sections.label: Defending multiracial multi-religious harmony
sections.summary: The speaker says Singapore's multiracial and multi-religious trust, unity and harmony must be defended, showing empathy for war victims without letting conflicts divide us.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: We have to defend this hard-earned multiracial and multi-religious trust, unity and harmony.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: We should show empathy for the victims of wars elsewhere, but we must never let such conflicts divide us.

sections.label: Flights and MFA assistance
sections.summary: Commercial flights and travel via neighbouring countries were available and MFA helped those facing challenges, though not every Singaporean overseas had eRegistered with MFA.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Thankfully, there were commercial flights still available, while others were able to get to neighbouring countries before flying out, and MFA was also in touch to help those who faced challenges.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: However, this was not as straightforward as it seemed, because not every Singaporean travelling overseas had eRegistered with MFA before going on their travels and it was always not easy for MFA to trace and get in touch with every Singaporean who may need assistance.

sections.label: Conflict fatalities and displacement figures
sections.summary: The speaker cites UN figures of almost 11,000 fatalities including children, women and elderly, and 1.4 million displaced in Gaza, with no end in sight.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: By any measure, it is hard to see an end in sight to this terrible conflict and going by how events have unfolded in the past month, it is clear that more lives will be lost in the coming days to weeks.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It was reported by the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs that, as of last Saturday, 4 November, Day 29 of the crisis, that among almost the 11,000 fatalities, 31 Israeli children out of 1,400 Israeli fatalities, 3,900 Palestinian children, 2,430 Palestinian women and 572 Palestinian elderly.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: One point four million have been displaced in Gaza, a land that is half the size of Singapore and, in relative terms, the number of deaths that the conflict has contributed in a mere 29 days and still counting, is fast approaching half of the total deaths that Singapore saw in a full year in 2022.

sections.label: Support for humanitarian truce
sections.summary: The speaker supports Singapore's UN vote for an immediate, durable and sustained humanitarian truce, aid access, civilian protection, and condemns terrorist acts and international law violations on both sides.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We are not yet sure how much further this crisis could unravel and the destabilising impact that it has in the wider Middle East and other regions of the world.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I support the Government's position, as outlined by Singapore's affirmative vote at the UN General Assembly on 27 October for an "immediate, durable and sustained humanitarian truce leading to a cessation of hostilities", a demand for aid access and a determined protection of civilians.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Singapore must continue to push for a ceasefire to come to fruition, for a sustained delivery of humanitarian aid to areas of conflict and to persist in its principled position of unequivocally condemning terrorist acts and violations of international law on both sides, and for the safety and security of civilians, including the release of all hostages.

sections.label: Speaker's Corner discussion disappointment
sections.summary: The speaker was disappointed the conflict could not be discussed more openly at the Speaker's Corner or public assemblies, and hopes the Government will reconsider sooner rather than later.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this regard, given the depth and richness of knowledge that the conflict could offer by way of national education and learning, I was slightly disappointed when it was announced that the topic of this conflict could not be discussed more openly at the Speaker's Corner or as part of events or public assemblies when, in fact, the matter was already widely covered and readily accessible online and in local newspapers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I can appreciate the initial concerns over public order, the sensitivity of the topic as well as the volatility of the situation overseas, but I do hope that the Government will reconsider this position in good time and I would suggest for this to be allowed sooner rather than later.

sections.label: Gaza, West Bank, wider conflict
sections.summary: The Motion focuses on the Israeli-Hamas conflict and Gaza, but the wider Israel-Palestine conflict includes the West Bank, where death, injury and property destruction have increased since 7 October.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As a whole, society then benefits and matures from such depth and nuance of discourse over time.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I conclude, Mr Deputy Speaker, that while this Motion is focused on the Israeli-Hamas conflict with a specific focus to the House on the recent devastation within Gaza, it should be noted that the wider conflict between Israel and Palestine also includes that of the West Bank, an area that spans about 15 times the size Gaza, where it remains the case that death, injury and destruction of property have also increased dramatically since 7 October.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, in this globalised and interconnected world, it is impossible and irresponsible for us to ignore the plight of people suffering all manner of injustice and devastation, illegal settlements where there is little access to food, water and electricity, and uncertainty about their lives tomorrow.

sections.label: Mufti on violence against civilians
sections.summary: Singapore has largely avoided polarisation due to principled stances of Muslim community leaders, and the Mufti stated there is no justification for violence against civilians by anyone, including Hamas or in retaliation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Singapore is not immune to these developments, but due to the principled stances taken by the leaders in our Muslim community, we have largely avoided polarisation between communities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I was deeply struck by what the Mufti of Singapore, Ustaz Nazirudin Mohd Nasir stated in his lefter to the Chief Rabbi of Singapore: He said: "There is no place or justification for any form of violence and brutality on civilians by anyone, including Hamas, or in any retaliatory response.

sections.label: Muslim community response and government position
sections.summary: Muslims accept developments should not affect harmony with fellow Singaporeans, draw on Singapore's UNGA votes since 1967 for a two-state solution, and respond with prayers, peace messages and assistance through credible channels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: At the same time, they accept that these developments should not affect the peace and harmony with fellow Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: They also drew succour from the Singapore Government's position expressed in voting for UNGA resolutions since 1967 which involved, amongst others, advocating for a two-state solution where both the states of Israel and Palestine are recognised; the refusal to recognise Jerusalem as the capital of Israel; condemning the illegal construction of settlements by Israel; and calling for an immediate and sustained humanitarian truce to the current crisis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Their response, collectively, has been in form of prayers for relief from the suffering of affected people; emphasising the Islamic message of peace, compassion, kindness and fairness; and providing assistance through trustworthy and credible channels to help those affected by the tragedy.

sections.label: Malay community and harmony
sections.summary: After independence the Malay community became a minority but embraced a Singapore for all races and religions, securing peace and harmony, and this spirit is exemplified in its approach to the Gaza crisis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: What may not have been sufficiently highlighted then and now is the fact that when Singapore became independent, our Malay community, which was the majority race before independence, became a minority race thereafter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Yet, our Malay community fully embraced the concept of a Singapore for all races and religions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Thankfully, as a result, we secured peace and harmony that contributed to the prosperity and progress of all our people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This spirit is once again exemplified by the responsible approach and stance that has been taken by our Muslim friends, particularly our Malay/Muslim community, in dealing with Gaza crisis.

sections.label: Offences for terrorism dealings
sections.summary: In Singapore it is an offence to deal with any individual or organisation for terrorist acts or to support terrorism, including financing, or to have financial dealings with a terrorist or terrorist entity under the Terrorism Suppression of Financing Act 2002.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: In Singapore, it is an offence for anyone to deal with any individual or organisation regardless of whether it is designated.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: If the purpose is for terrorist act or otherwise to support terrorism, including the financing of terrorism.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: It is also an offence to have financial dealings with any individual or organisation that meets the definition of a terrorist or terrorist entity under the Terrorism Suppression of Financing Act 2002, even if it is not specifically designated in the First Schedule.

sections.label: Definition of terrorist act
sections.summary: The passage lists actions constituting a terrorist act, including serious violence, damage, endangerment, firearms, hazardous substances, disruption of computer systems and emergency services, and prejudice to public security, and says Hamas's actions fulfil that definition.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Just to summarise, to give you a flavour of the actions: serious violence against a person; serious damage of property; endangering a person's life; serious risk to the health and safety of the public; use of firearms and explosives; involving the release into the environment any dangerous, hazardous, radioactive or harmful substance, any toxic chemical, any microbiological or toxin; disrupts and seriously interferes with any public computer system or services related to infrastructure, banking, financial services, public utilities; disrupts or interferes with the provision of essential emergency services; involves prejudice to public security and national defence; and where the use or threat of these actions is intended to either influence or compel the Government or any other government or any international organisation to do or refrain from doing any such act or to intimidate the public or section of the public.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I think it is very clear what Hamas did would certainly fulfil that definition of a terrorist act and have no doubt it would not be allowed in Singapore, neither to finance or support or to get involved.

sections.label: Singapore position on two-state solution
sections.summary: Singapore has consistently held that the two-state solution is right and settlements are illegal.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I hope that illustrates the point that Singapore has taken a consistent position throughout all these years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: We still believe in the two-state solution, that the settlements are illegal and the sooner that it is resolved, the better.

sections.label: Hamas 7 October attack
sections.summary: The 7 October Hamas action was a planned terrorist attack that massacred civilians and took hostages.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: First, what happened on 7 October by Hamas was a planned and coordinated terrorist attack – the brutal massacre of civilians and the taking of civilian hostages.

sections.label: Israel's right to defend itself
sections.summary: Israel has a legitimate right to defend itself.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Second, Israel has a legitimate right to defend itself.

sections.label: Singapore support for humanitarian truce
sections.summary: Singapore supported the latest UN resolution calling for a humanitarian truce leading to cessation of hostilities.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Our heart goes out to the Palestinian people.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: That is why Singapore supported the latest UN resolution calling for a humanitarian truce, leading to a cessation of hostilities.

sections.label: Negotiated two-state solution
sections.summary: Singapore's support for a two-state solution is unchanged, and negotiation is the only way to peace.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Meanwhile, Singapore's long-standing support for a two-state solution remains unchanged.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: A negotiated two-state solution is the only way for Palestinians and Israelis to live in peace and security.

sections.label: Reports of offensive remarks in Singapore
sections.summary: In October police received eight reports of offensive remarks against Jewish or Muslim communities, nearly the prior nine months' total.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In the month of October alone, the Police received eight reports of offensive remarks or actions targeted at members of the Jewish or Muslim communities in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Eight may not seem like a large number to you, but in just this one month of October, we have received almost the same number of related reports as we did in the preceding nine months of the year combined.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: That is why we cannot afford to be complacent.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We know from our own painful history how disastrous ethnic and religious strife can be.

sections.label: Economic impact of Israel-Hamas conflict
sections.summary: Direct economic impact is small due to limited trade and investment linkages, but a broader regional conflict would affect oil and food prices, so plans are being updated.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: For now, the direct economic impact is small, because of our limited trade and investment linkages with Israel and Palestine.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But should the conflict between Israel and Hamas broaden into a regional conflict in the Middle East, there will certainly be wider implications, especially on oil and food prices.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, we must be prepared for more uncertainties ahead and we are updating our drawer plans should the situation take a turn for the worse and we are impacted.

sections.label: Detentions and online radicalisation threats
sections.summary: Singaporeans have been detained for pro-Hamas narratives and attack plans, and regional extremist Internet traffic and anti-Singapore rhetoric have risen since the conflict started.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Members all know that in recent years, we have detained Singaporeans who fell for pro-Hamas narratives and wanted to take up arms overseas.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We have had radicalised individuals who have also planned attacks on Singaporean targets and since the conflict started, regional Internet traffic on extremist sites has already gone up three-fold – because we track these sites, we know the traffic has increased and we have also observed an uptick in anti-Singapore rhetoric, including violent threats against Singapore by regional extremist elements online.

sections.label: Mufti on peaceful co-existence
sections.summary: The Mufti said work for a model of peaceful co-existence in Singapore has become more critical and achieving peaceful relations is the greatest urgency.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Mufti said and I quote: "Our work to put forth a different model of peaceful co-existence, where every community in Singapore can live peacefully alongside other faiths and celebrate diversity, has now become even more critical… Despite the overwhelming challenges, achieving peaceful relations is not impossible and is now the greatest urgency." And I cannot agree more with him.

sections.label: Call to steward peace and harmony
sections.summary: The speaker urges every Singaporean and Member to be good stewards of peace and harmony and to stand together as one united people.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We understand and share in one another's festive celebrations, all of us proud of our multiracial, multi-religious Singaporean identity.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, to every Singaporean, to every Member of this House, I say let us be good stewards, good stewards of our peace and harmony.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Let us work at it consistently, assiduously, daily and let us stand together, now more than ever, as one united people.

sections.label: Government omissions on Israel-Hamas position
sections.summary: The speaker says the Government treated it as a national security matter and did not take the House into confidence on its Israel-Hamas position.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: My second point really is about something a bit more fundamental – which Deputy Prime Minister spoke about.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: He talked about it being a national security matter, that there was an impression that the Government had – that there were some omissions which were quite critical.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: The Government did not take us into confidence on its position on the Israel-Hamas issue.

sections.label: WP condemning Hamas and national security confidence
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes posting the speeches, seeks a clear WP condemnation of Hamas terrorism, and says the WP will be taken into confidence on national security concerns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I am glad that he will be posting his speech and Mr Giam's speech on the website.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
