sentences.text: I think what is more important is not just the speech themselves but a clear position from the WP that it condemns unequivocable the acts of terrorism by Hamas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And on national security, I fully take on board the points that he has raised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We will and we have been, and we will continue to do this from time to time when indeed there are national security concerns, we take the WP into confidence, we share what they and we would appreciate very much across all political parties, whatever our backgrounds, we stand united as Singaporeans because on such matters, there can be nothing that divides us.

sections.label: Victims on both sides
sections.summary: It acknowledges victims on both sides of the conflict and that both sides should protect civilians and deliver humanitarian aid.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Second, it acknowledges that there are victims on both sides of the conflict and that both sides should ensure the protection of civilians and the delivery of humanitarian aid.

sections.label: Rise in Islamophobia reported
sections.summary: The Council on American-Islamic Relations reported a rise in Islamophobia, with incidents and requests for help spiking 182% since the Hamas attacks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Meanwhile, the Council on American-Islamic Relations reported a rise in Islamophobia with incidents and requests for help spiking by 182% since the Hamas attacks.

sections.label: Hamas 2017 Charter aims
sections.summary: Hamas' 2017 Charter declares the state of Israel illegal and illegitimate and states its aim is the elimination of Israel.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Hamas' 2017 Charter declares the state of Israel as illegal and illegitimate and states that its aim is the elimination of Israel.

sections.label: Two-state solution support
sections.summary: It states freedom to practise religion, build homes and families, grow economy, society and culture, and stand proudly can only be achieved through a two-state solution the Motion supports.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To have the freedom to practise their own religion, to build homes and families and to grow their economy, society and culture and to stand proudly amongst the people of the world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This can only be achieved through a two-state solution that this Motion reiterates Singapore's support for.

sections.label: Rahmatan Lil Alamin Foundation funds
sections.summary: The Rahmatan Lil Alamin Foundation raised over $4.5 million in less than two weeks to provide healthcare supplies and shelter for those affected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For example, the Rahmatan Lil Alamin Foundation has raised over $4.5 million in less than two weeks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These funds will be used to provide healthcare supplies and shelter for those affected in this conflict.

sections.label: MUIS religious advisory
sections.summary: MUIS is developing a religious advisory to guide Muslims here on responses to overseas conflicts and has been engaging the Muslim community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this regard, I was heartened to read that the Majlis Ugama Islam Singapura (MUIS) is developing a religious advisory to guide Muslims here on the response to overseas conflicts, such as the current conflict, and has been actively engaging the Muslim community to provide an understanding of the conflict from the local religious perspective.

sections.label: Pope Francis fasting prayer call
sections.summary: Pope Francis called for a day of fasting and prayer on 27 October 2023 to intercede for an end to the Israel-Hamas war.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: His Holiness Pope Francis called for a day of fasting and prayer on 27 October 2023 to intercede for an end to the Israel-Hamas war.

sections.label: Attack and Israeli military response
sections.summary: The 7 October attack killed 1,400 soldiers and many civilians and was condemned globally, while Israel's military response killed more than 9,000 Palestinians, including children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Fellow Parliamentarians here have already shared how the attack on 7 October, which killed 1,400 soldiers and many civilians, has been rightfully condemned globally.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: However, Israel's military response has killed more than 9,000 Palestinians, including children.

sections.label: Singapore UN humanitarian truce vote
sections.summary: Singapore supported a UN resolution on 27 October calling for an immediate and sustained humanitarian truce, protection of civilians and unhindered essential supplies to Gaza civilians.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: We must advocate a humanitarian truce and ensure the immediate delivery of aid to the civilian population in Gaza.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: It was, indeed, imperative that on 27 October, Singapore took an unequivocal stand and expressed its concerns over the situation in Gaza by supporting the UN resolution calling for an immediate and sustained humanitarian truce, emphasising that civilians must be protected in accordance with international humanitarian law and international human rights law and the immediate and unhindered provision of essential supplies to civilians in Gaza.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Singapore stood firm with many from the rest of the world in favour of a non-binding resolution drafted by the Arab states, even when 44 other countries abstained from voting and 14 voted against it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The conflict draws much regional and international attention, as competing stakeholders safeguard their own interests.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: It would be naive of anyone to assume that a solution is easy and Singapore has always supported a two-state solution and our vote on 27 October in the UN resolution reaffirms that stand.

sections.label: Teo Chee Hean Palestinian Authority visit
sections.summary: On 10 July, Senior Minister Teo Chee Hean called on the Palestinian Authority's Prime Minister in Ramallah, reaffirming warm ties and support through the $10-million Enhanced Technical Assistance Package.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: More recently, on 10 July, Senior Minister Teo Chee Hean called on the Palestinian Authority's Prime Minister during his visit to Ramallah, reaffirming the warm ties between Singapore and the Palestinian Authority.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: We must continue to support capability building for the Palestinians, such as through the $10-million Enhanced Technical Assistance Package (ETAP), which has benefited more than 600 Palestinian officials in courses on public administration, technical and vocational education, and training and economic development.

sections.label: Attack deaths and Palestinian deaths
sections.summary: The globally condemned terrorist attack killed 1,400 military personnel and civilians, and Israel's military response killed more than 9,000 Palestinians including more than 3,000 children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Ever since the terrorist attack, which was condemned globally, killed 1,400 military personnel and civilians, Israel's military response has killed more than 9,000 Palestinians including more than 3,000 children.

sections.label: Singapore support for UN resolution
sections.summary: On 27 October, Singapore supported the UN resolution to condemn all acts of violence to civilians, call for an immediate humanitarian truce and ensure protection of civilians and delivery of humanitarian aid.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Therefore, many of our people want the hostilities to stop, so that humanitarian aid can be rendered in Gaza.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Therefore, it is important that on 27 October, Singapore took a firm stand and expressed our concern over the situation in Gaza by supporting the UN resolution to condemn all acts of violence to civilians regardless of race, call for an immediate humanitarian truce and cessation of hostilities, ensure the protection of civilians and delivery of humanitarian aid immediately without any hindrance.

sections.label: Pasir Ris resident on conflict
sections.summary: A Pasir Ris resident said the conflict is a political conflict causing humanitarian issues, resolvable only by a two-state solution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: A resident of Pasir Ris, Madam Syaazwani Ahmad, said, "It is clear now that this is an issue of political conflict that have resulted in humanitarian issues." The conflict can only be resolved through a two-state solution.

sections.label: UN vote on illegal settlements
sections.summary: Singapore previously supported the vote against illegal settlements in the Occupied Palestinian Territories as it violates international law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Just like what we did at the UN resolution on 27 Oct, we had also previously supported the vote against illegal settlements in the Occupied Palestinian Territories as it also violates international law.

sections.label: ETAP Programme and PA capability
sections.summary: Minister Maliki reaffirmed support for the ETAP Programme, to which Singapore allocated S$10 million and trained over 600 Palestinian officials.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: With that, I am heartened to hear Minister Maliki answering my Parliamentary Question and reaffirming his continued support for the ETAP Programme to further support the building of the PA capability in which Singapore has allocated S$10 million and has trained more than 600 Palestinian officials.

sections.label: RLAF and Humanity Matters fundraising
sections.summary: Fundraising by RLAF and Humanity Matters, working together to unite people, enables more effective assistance to the humanitarian crisis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Efforts such as fund raising efforts by RLAF and Humanity Matters in which we work together to unite our people will enable us to make a more effective impact in rendering assistance to this humanitarian crisis.

sections.label: Staying together to assist Gaza
sections.summary: Staying together is how the situation in Gaza can best be assisted as the world works towards a long-lasting two-state solution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Staying together is how we can best assist the situation in Gaza as the world continues to work towards a long-lasting two-state solution.

sections.label: Singapore's support for UN resolution
sections.summary: Singapore supported the 26 October 2023 UN resolution with 119 nations, calling for a humanitarian truce and respect for international law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Singapore supported the recent UN resolution on 26 October 2023, entitled "Protection of civilians and upholding legal and humanitarian obligations", along with 119 member nations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This resolution calls for an immediate, durable and sustained humanitarian truce leading to a cessation of hostilities as well as for all parties to respect international law.

sections.label: Government seed funding and donations
sections.summary: Singapore contributed an initial $300,000 from the Government, and about $5 million in total has now been received.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Singapore started by contributing an initial seed amount from the Government of $300,000, and as updated by the Minister earlier, about $5 million in total has now been received, and many other initiatives are also underway.

sections.label: Religious guidance and churches praying
sections.summary: Religious leaders must give correct guidance, and the National Council of Churches of Singapore called churches to pray for the Israel-Palestinian conflict.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Religious leaders must do everything in their means to give correct guidance as ultimately all faiths subscribe to the principles of love, respect, kindness, compassion and peace.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Fellow Christians in Singapore are deeply saddened by the loss of innocent lives in this conflict and by the suffering that inevitably accompanies conflict.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The National Council of Churches of Singapore has called the churches in Singapore to pray for the Israel-Palestinian conflict.

sections.label: UN resolution and national consensus
sections.summary: The speaker supports the UN General Assembly resolution of 27 October 2023 calling for a humanitarian truce and is proud of Singapore's vote in favour.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: And equally so, the important need for all Singaporeans to have a consensus and common view on our national interests.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: So, while I fully support the resolution passed by the 10th Emergency Special Session of the UN General Assembly on 27 October 2023 calling for, I quote, "an immediate, durable and sustained humanitarian truce leading to a cessation of hostilities", so as to allow the "full, immediate, safe, unhindered and sustained access to humanitarian aid to respond to the most basic needs of the Palestinian civilian population in the Gaza Strip", and while I am proud of Singapore's vote in favour of this resolution, let us also be very clear.

sections.label: Hamas acts of terror
sections.summary: What Hamas did in Southern Israel on 7 October 2023 are acts of terror.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: What Hamas did in Southern Israel on 7 October 2023 are acts of terror.

sections.label: Canada's proposed UN amendment
sections.summary: Canada proposed an amendment to also reject and condemn the Hamas attacks starting 7 October 2023 and the taking of hostages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: It is in our absolute national interest to have a clear consensus in this House on this point.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: It matters, because in the UN General Assembly 10th Emergency Special Session, Canada did propose an amendment to resolution that was passed, to also "unequivocally reject and condemn the terrorist attacks by Hamas that took place in Israel starting on 7 October 2023 and the taking of hostages".

sections.label: Singapore supports UN ceasefire resolution
sections.summary: The UN Special Emergency Meeting passed a resolution calling for an immediate and sustained humanitarian ceasefire, and Singapore supports it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin): The United Nations Special Emergency Meeting on the Israel-Hamas war passed a resolution calling for an immediate and sustained humanitarian ceasefire by both sides, to facilitate the cessation of hostilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Singapore supports this resolution at the United Nations.

sections.label: UN resolution and self-defence
sections.summary: Singapore's support for the UN resolution is support for international law, though the resolution does not mention a country's right to self-defence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Singapore's support for the UN resolution is support for international law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: However, we must also emphasise that the UN resolution does not mention a country's right to self-defence under international law.

sections.label: Singapore votes on Israel resolutions
sections.summary: Singapore voted against Jerusalem as Israel's capital in 2017, opposed illegal settlements in 2022, and recently supported a Gaza humanitarian resolution.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In 2017, we voted against Jerusalem being made the capital of Israel.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In 2022, we were against the illegal settlements by Israel and asserted that it was against international law.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Recently, we have supported a resolution that calls for an immediate humanitarian assistance and provision of essential supplies to civilians in Gaza.

sections.label: Solidarity with civilian conflict victims
sections.summary: It calls for standing united with innocent civilians in the Israel-Hamas conflict and upholding peace, justice and humanitarianism.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: As we stand in unison with the innocent civilian lives caught in the crossfire of the Israel-Hamas conflict, let us also stand united in our resolve to uphold values of peace, justice and humanitarianism.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Let the narrative of solidarity security and peace resonate across our lands, reminding us of our shared responsibility towards fostering a harmonious community.

sections.label: Police reports on offensive remarks
sections.summary: In October 2023 the Singapore Police Force received eight reports of offensive remarks or actions against Jewish or Muslim communities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: As mentioned by Deputy Prime Minister Wong earlier, in the month of October 2023 alone, the Singapore Police Force received eight reports of offensive remarks or actions targeted at either members of the Jewish or Muslim communities in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: This is equal to the total number of anti-Semitic or anti-Muslim police reports received between January and September this year.

sections.label: Rejected Israel-Hamas event applications
sections.summary: Five rejected applications were to hold events related to the Israel-Hamas conflict in October 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Five of the rejected applications were to hold events related to the Israel-Hamas conflict in October 2023.

sections.label: Condemning terrorism and violence
sections.summary: Singapore condemns all acts of terrorism and will not tolerate people calling for violence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong mentioned the individuals we had detained in the past.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Our stance is clear – we condemn all acts of terrorism.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Neither will we tolerate people calling for violence.

sections.label: Standing Order 48(3) speech limits
sections.summary: The Speaker reminds Members that under Standing Order 48(3) only the mover may speak more than once on a Motion, and asks for concise points of clarification and questions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: In fact, there has been an occasion where the mini-speech exceeded five minutes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: So, I want to remind Members that under Standing Order 48(3), no Member other than the mover is allowed to speak more than once on a Motion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Making a point of clarification or asking supplementary questions are not further occasions for a second speech.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: I will allow some leeway for Members to explain their point of clarification or make their question intelligible, but I ask Members for your cooperation and understanding to observe the Standing Orders and to keep your points of clarifications and questions concise and to the point.

sections.label: UN humanitarian truce resolution
sections.summary: The second and third components of the debate give substance to the humanitarian crisis, following a UN resolution for an immediate, durable and sustained humanitarian truce and cessation of hostilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: The second and third components of this debate are where we give substance to the humanitarian crisis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: There was a UN resolution passed for immediate, durable and sustained humanitarian truce and a call for cessation, leading to the cessation of hostilities.

sections.label: Violations of international law
sections.summary: The second component concerns violations of international law, which must be condemned regardless of the party responsible, including the principles of distinction, proportionality and positive obligations to protect civilians.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: The second component – the violations of international law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: This also has to be condemned, regardless of which party is responsible, and the relevant principles of international law include the principles applicable to arm conflict including the principle of distinction, which means civilians and civilian objects cannot be made targets of military attack; proportionality, which means any response has to be proportionate to the threat; as well as positive obligations to protect civilians and civilian objects from the effects of war.

sections.label: Call for hostage release
sections.summary: The call for the release of hostages is universal, and there is no excuse for keeping hostages, who must be released immediately.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: There is some overlap between this and the earlier limbs, but I think the call for release of hostages is also universal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: There is no excuse for keeping hostages and they have to be released immediately.

sections.label: Capacity building with Palestinian Authority
sections.summary: Several speakers, including Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong, Dr Vivian Balakrishnan, Dr Maliki and Mr Sharael Taha, highlighted efforts to engage in capacity building with the Palestinian Authority and help build up their skills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: With the Palestinians, several speakers including Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong, Dr Vivian Balakrishnan, Dr Maliki and Mr Sharael Taha have highlighted the efforts that we have taken to engage in capacity building with the Palestinian Authority, and to continue to help them build up their skills.

sections.label: Rise in hate crimes
sections.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong and Senior Parliamentary Secretary Faisal Ibrahim highlighted rising complaints about hate crimes in Singapore, while Mr Raj Joshua Thomas noted a worldwide rise and Singapore's vulnerability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: Both Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong and Senior Parliamentary Secretary Faisal Ibrahim highlighted the complaints about hate crimes have been on the rise in Singapore, although the numbers are still small while Mr Raj Joshua Thomas highlighted a rise in hate crimes across the world and indicated that Singapore may also be vulnerable.

sections.label: Mufti condemns violence against civilians
sections.summary: The Mufti said there is no justification for violence and brutality on civilians by anyone, including Hamas or in retaliation, and offered condolences and solidarity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: After the attack, the Mufti Ustaz Dr Nazirudin Mohd Nasir in his letter, "There is no place and no justification for any form of violence and brutality on civilians by anyone, including by Hamas, or in any retaliatory response." He also offered his sincerest condolences, prayers and solidarity to those whose lives are unjustly taken.

sections.label: Proposed amendments on humanitarian truce
sections.summary: Amendment No 1 supports UN Resolution ES-10/21 calling for an immediate humanitarian truce leading to cessation of hostilities; Amendment No 2 adds unhindered access to humanitarian agencies; Amendment No 4 inserts compliance with international humanitarian law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Amendment No 1 is, "After line 4, to insert a new part with the words 'Supports UN Resolution ES-10/21, which calls for an immediate, durable and sustained humanitarian truce leading to a cessation of hostilities'".

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Amendment No 2 is, "In line 5, the words 'and unhindered access to United Nations humanitarian agencies, the International Red Cross and other humanitarian organisations' be added at the end".

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Amendment No 4 is, "In line 7, after the words 'all parties to', to insert the following: 'comply fully with international humanitarian law, including to'".
